title: Series backends
preamble:
# Series backends

The **aggregation backends** behind the samples plane, as an integrator meets
them. A backend is the code that maintains a series' sliding state (mean,
sliding min/max, count-distinct, …) and answers queries. This is a distinct
surface from the samples-plane *observation* callbacks in
[NSTG.5]: those forward absorbed samples *out* to
your storage; a backend computes the aggregation the rules read.

Every backend is libds's own. The seven of [NSBK.6.1] are compiled into
`libds.a` and registered by libds when it constructs an engine; an integrator
supplies and registers none ([NSBK.2.3]). What an integrator meets of them is
here: which backings exist, their identities in the platform signature, and
the integrator's read. How libds shapes them is the impl tree's
[ISBK].

## What this is not

- Not the samples-plane observation surface — see [NSTG.5]
  (`sample_cb` / `series_declared_cb`).
- Not the author-side series language — see
  [LSER].
- Not the algorithm catalogue. The bundled algorithms document themselves.
- Not an extension point. No external backend is admitted ([NSBK.2.3]).
